lawyer:
Mr. Md. Abdul Awal, Advocate, For the petitioners. 
Mr. Bazlur Rashid, Advocate, For the opposite party.
parties:
Md. Delwar Hossain Molla alias Dilu Molla and others.
Vs.
Abul Kashem Molla being dead his heirs Md. Salim Molla and others.
full_judgment:
Mahmudul Haque, J: This Rule, on an application under section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure (in short, the Code) was issued at the instance of the defendant–appellant-petitioners calling upon the opposite party no.1 to show cause as to why the impugned judgment and decree dated 20.03.2008 passed by the Additional District Judge, Patuakhali in Title Appeal No. 11 of 2006 affirming the judgment and decree dated 13.11.2005 passed by the Joint District Judge, First Court, Patuakhali in Title Suit No. 16 of 2001 decreeing the suit should not be set aside and/ or such other or further order or orders passed as to this Court may seem fit and proper.

2. The facts relevant for disposal of the Rule, in short, are that the present opposite party no. 1, Abul Kashem Molla (now dead) filed Title Suit no. 16 of 2001 initially against the defendant nos. 1-8, later on, defendant nos. 9-22 were added in the suit for partition of the suit land described in the schedule `ka' to the plaint.

3. The plaintiff asserted in the plaint that 4.58 acres of land appertain to RS plot no. 2381, 8.47 acres of R.S plot no. 2386 under RS khatian no. 36 and 5.62 acres under plot no. 2418 and 5.18 acres under plot no. 2419 of RS khatian no. 47 of Londa Mouja were the subject matter of Title Suit No. 40 of 1954 of Subordinate Judge, Second Court, Barishal.

4. In the said suit (Title Suit No. 40 of 1954) the plaintiff Abul Kashem Molla was defendant no. 13 and his sister Mominjan was defendant no. 12. The said title suit was decreed on compromise on 23.04.1954 in preliminary form and the said decree was made final on 26.04.1954. The defendant nos. 12 and 13 (Mominjan and present plaintiff Abul Kashem Molla) of that suit got 2.86 acres of land from plot no. 2381 and 3.25 acres of land from plot no. 2386 of RS khatian No. 36 and 3.17 acres of land from plot no. 2418 and 2.85 acres of land from plot no. 2419 of RS khatian No. 47 in their saham, that is, in total defendant nos. 12 and 13 of the said suit got 12.13 acres of land in their share and pursuant to the said decree the defendant nos. 12 and 13 were possessing, the said land with the knowledge of all.

5. The plaintiff got 50% of the said decretal land measuring an area of 6.065 acres. The plaintiff has dwelling hut, pond and garden on plot no. 2386 of RS khatian No. 36.

6. Mominjan (the defendant no. 13) died leaving brothers, plaintiff Abul Kashem Molla, Hafizur Rahman (defendant no. 1) and full sister Ambia Khatun, defendant no. 2. Plaintiff got 2.42 acres of land from the share of Mominjan, thus the plaintiff has acquired 8.485 acres of land.

7. The plaintiff has been facing some problem to possess and develop his land with the co-sharers jointly as the land has not been partitioned among them by metes and bounds till now.

8. The plaintiff requested the co-sharers for partition of the land but they refused to do the same. It is also asserted in the plaint that the government constructed embankment in the area which is known as WAPDA embankment and in the said WAPDA embankment the government acquired .305 acres of land from the share of the plaintiff, so the plaintiff is entitled to get a saham for his remaining 8.18 acres of land in his share. The defendant no. 1 denied to partition the suit land amicably, finally on 20th Chaitra, 1407 BS, thus the plaintiff has been constrained to file the present suit.

9. The defendant nos. 8 and 18-21 filed two separate written statements but ultimately the suit was contested by defendant nos. 18-21 and the defendant no. 1 prayed for saham only.

10. In the written statements of defendant nos. 18-21 among others it was averred that the suit is not maintainable in its present form; the plaintiff has no cause of action for filing of the suit; all the co-sharers have not been made party in the suit and all the lands of the co-sharers has not been brought into the schedule as such, the suit in suffers from defect of hotchpotch and the claim of the plaintiff is also false.

11. The case of the defendant nos. 18-21 is that the plaintiff Abul Kashem Molla and his sister Mominjan had two full brothers, their names are Abdul Ha.mid and Hafizur Rahman. Abul Kashem Molla and his sister Mominjan in collusion with the plaintiff of Title Suit No. 40 of 1954 made them defendants in the said suit leaving the two full brothers, Abdul Hamid and Hafizur Rahman and also obtained the decree collusively for their illegal gain although the lands belonged to Abul Kashem Mollah, Mominjan, Abdul Ham id and Hafizur Rahman.

12. The 3 full brothers, Abul Kashem Molla, Abdul Hamid and Md. Hafizur Ra.hman and their full sister Mominjan got settlement of 12.13 acres of land from the plaintiff of Title Suit No. 40 of 1954.Later on, Abdul Hamid, the predecessor of defendant nos. 18-21, Hafizur Rahman the present plaintiff Abul Kashem Molla and their sister Mominjan jointly filed Title Suit No. 190 of 1956 in the Court of the then Subordinate Judge, Second Court, Barishal for declaration of their title and the said suit was also decreed on compromise on 11.12.1956. Since Abul Kashem Molla was one of the plaintiff of Title Suit No. 190 of 1956 he cannot avoid the judgment and decree of Title Suit No. 190 of 1956 and he cannot rely upon the decree passed in Title Suit No. 40 of 1954 denying the decree passed in Title Suit No. 190 of 1956. So, the suit of the plaintiff is liable to be dismissed. Since the other defendants ultimately did not contest in the suit I find no reason to aver their case.

13. On the above pleadings, the trial Court framed issues and the plaintiff upon the issues framed, examined 3 witnesses and submitted some papers which were marked as exhibit nos. 1, 1(Ka) and 2 while the contesting defendant nos. 18-21 examined one witness and submitted the decree and the plaint in Title Suit No. 190 of 1956 which were marked as exhibit 'Ka' series.

14. The trial Court considering the evidence adduced by the parties and relying upon the decree of Title Suit No. 40 of 1954 decreed the suit in preliminary form on 13.11.2005 allotting a saham for 8.18 acres of land in favour of plaintiff, Abul Kashem Mollah and 2.42 acres of land in favour of the defendant no. 1 with a direction to partition the land amicably within 60 days failing which parties will be entitled to get the land partitioned through Court.

15. The defendant nos. 18-21 being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the said judgment of the trial Court dated 13.11.2005 filed Title Appeal No. 11 of 2006 in the Court of District Judge, Patuakhali which was ultimately heard by the Additional district Judge, Patuakhali on transfer who by his impugned judgment and decree dated 20.03.2008 disallowed the appeal affirming the judgment of the trial Court. The defendant nos. 18-21 as against the said judgment of the appellate Court below moved this Court by filing this application under section 115(1) of the Code and obtained the present Rule as stated hereinbefore.

16. On the date of issuance of the Rule the operation of the impugned judgment and decree dated 20.3.2008 were stayed till disposal of this Rule.

17. The Rule is contested by the heirs of the opposite party no. 1 as opposite party nos. 1(a) to 1(h). During pendency of this Rule the petitioners (defendant nos. 18-21 of the original suit) filed an additional written statement and also filed another application under Order 41 Rule 27 (1) b of the Code for accepting additional evidence. The opposite party no.1 by filing an affidavit-in-opposition opposed the Rule and the revisional application as a whole.

18. Mr. Md. Abdul Awal, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner submits that the judgment of the appellate Court below is a dazzling instance of miscarriage of justice and non-application of judicial mind of the author judge of the impugned judgment who blindly followed the judgment of the trial Court. The appellate Court below without perusing the records and judgment of the Court below decided the fate of the appeal by his banal and trite judgment occasioning failure of justice.

19. The learned Advocate for the petitioners also submits that Title Suit No. 40 of 1954 was filed by some other persons and there were more than 106.00 acres of land in the schedule. In the said suit Mominjan and Abul Kashem Molla were made defendant Nos. 12 and 13. They did not (defendant nos. 12 and 13) file the said suit and the nature of the suit, its filing, service of summons and decree itself are sufficient to hold that the plaintiff of that suit had no knowledge as to who were the owners and who have been possessing the huge 106.00 acres of land.

20. The learned Advocate also submits that the suit was filed with some motive to obtain a decree from a Court of law, as a result, the plaintiff of that suit stated the fact of the suit in his own way where the defendant nos. 12 and 13 have been shown as the owner of 12.13 acres of land, in fact, that land was acquired by 3 full brothers and one sister, they are Abdul Hamid, Hafizur Rahman and Abul Kashem Molla (plaintiff of the present suit) and Mominjan Bibi.

21. The learned Advocate also submits that Title Suit No. 40 of 1954 was filed on 12.04.1954 in the Court and without waiting for service of return of summons solenama was filed on 15.04.1954 within 3 days of its filing and preliminary decree was passed on the basis of so called solenama on 23.04.1956 and decree was made final on 26.04.1954. The learned Advocate thus submits that within 14 days a suit for 106.00 acres of land was decreed in the name of the various persons and such a solenama might have been prepared at the time of filing of the suit, so the trial Court should not have relied upon such a decree which was passed within 14 days only. Over and again, the suit was not filed by Abul Kashem Molla and Mominjan Bibi rather it was filed by some other persons who may not have knowledge about the acquisition of suit land by 3 brothers and their full sister.

22. The learned Advocate also submits that whenever the 3 brothers and sister subsequently, filed Title Suit No. 190 of 1956 in the same Court of Barishal for declaration of their title jointly with reference to the decree passed in Title Suit No. 40 of 1954 and their settlement has been admitted by the landlord in the said suit. So, the decree of Title Suit No. 190 of 1956 is not antagonistic to the decree of Title Suit No. 40 of 1954 rather, since 3 brothers and 1 sister had filed Title Suit No. 190 of 1956 for declaration of their title and since the said suit was decreed, the decree of Title Suit No. 190 of 1956 will get more preference upon the decree of Title Suit No. 40 of 1954 and the decree of Title Suit No. 40 of 1954 so far it relates to the brother and their 1 sister have been merged with the decree of Title Suit No. 190 of 1956.

23. The learned Advocate also submits that the trial Court below relied much upon the decree of Title Suit No. 40 of 1954 since its original record was called for and came in the Court for its perusal, and did not rely upon the certified copy of decree and plaint of Title Suit No. 190 of 1956 as the original record was not called for by the defendant nos. 18-21, but after filing of Title Appeal No. 11 of 2006, the defendant nos. 18-21 (as appellants) to remove any sort of suspicion and cloud regarding the decree passed in Title Suit No. 190 of 1956 called for the original records of the said suit from the Barishal record room and though the record of Title Suit No. 190 of 1956 was received by the appellate Court below on 10.03.2008, the appellate Court below without going through the same disallowed the appeal by its judgment dated 20.03.2008 agreeing with the judgment of the trial court.

24. The learned Advocate also submits that in the said judgment the appellate Court below unfortunately relied upon the findings and observations of the trial Court and also held that the decree of the Title Suit No. 190 of 1956 is not believable without calling for the records whereas original record of Title Suit No. 190 of 1956 was lying with the Appellate Court.

25. The learned Advocate also submits that from the judgment of the appellate Court below it clearly appears that the appellate Court did not take notice of the tagging of the record of Title Suit No. 190 of 1956 with the record of Title Appeal No. 11 of 2006.The appellate Court below without going through the record of Title Suit No. 190 of 1956 did the same job like the trial Court that the decree of Title Suit No. 190 of 1956 is not believable relying on its certified copy only.

26. Thus the learned Advocate also submits that had the record of Title Suit No. 190 of 1956 been perused by the appellate Court below the decisions would have been otherwise but unfortunately, the appellate Court below without going through the record of Title Suit No. 190 of 1956 made a ditto to the judgment passed by the trial Court, thus it is a case of non-consideration of materials and evidence on record by the appellate Court below occasioning serious failure of justice.

27. The learned Advocate also submits that pursuant to the decree in Title Suit No. 190 of 1956, 3 brothers and their sister had mutated their names in the record of rights which ultimately established that the decree of Title Suit No. 40 of 1954 was not acted upon, moreover it was obtained at the instance of others having no actual knowledge of Abul Kashem Molla and Mominjan bibi.

28. The learned Advocate also submits that during the trial defendant nos. 18-21 could not submit those papers of mutation but at the time of hearing of this revision they filed the same as additional evidence. The learned Advocate also submits that they have filed an additional written statement in this Rule claiming their saham also.

29. The learned Advocate in his concluding submissions submits that both the decrees are liable to be set aside for non-consideration of the materials on record adduced by the defendant petitioners.

30. On the other hand Mr. Bazlur Rashid, learned Advocate appearing for the opposite party nos.1(a) -1(h) the Rule submits that it is fact that Abul Kashem Molla, Md. Abdul Hamid, Hafizur Rahman and Mominjan Bibi are the full brothers and sister but through Title Suit No. 40 of 1954 the suit land has been fallen in the share of Abul Kashem Molla and Mominjan Bibi and since Mominjan Bibi died leaving full brother Abul Kashem Molla and Hafizur Rahman and since the decretal land has not been partitioned by metes and bounds and since the defendant no. 1 denied to partition the land amicably, the plaintiff Abul Kashem Molla under compelling circumstances filed the suit in question claiming partition of the schedule land.

31. The learned Advocate for the opposite party also submits that Title Suit No. 190 of 1956 might have been filed and decreed but the decree of Title Suit No. 40 of 1954 has not been cancelled through the decree of Title Suit No. 190 of 1956. The plaintiff Abul Kashem Molla has been possessing the suit land on the basis of the decree passed in Title Suit No. 40 of 1954 and the plaintiff of the present suit successfully proved their right, title and interest in the suit land both before the trial Court and the appellate Court below and both the Courts below considering the materials on record rightly decreed the suit which do not call for any interference by this Court.

32. The learned Advocate also submits that the additional evidence filed in this Rule should not be accepted as the defendants could have filed the same in the trial Court or even in the appellate Court below. The learned Advocate also submits that defendants did not pray for any saham neither in the trial Court nor in the appellate Court so the said application is not entertainable at this stage. The learned Advocate in his concluding submissions submits that the Rule is liable to be discharged.

33. I have considered the above submissions of the learned Advocates of both the parties with profound attention and have gone through the materials on record particularly the record of Title Suit No. 16 of 2001 filed by Abul Kashem Molla whose heirs are opposite party nos. 1(a)-1(h) in this Rule, the record of Title Appeal No. 11 of 2006 and the records of two former suits being Title Suit No. 40 of 1954 and 190 of 1956 decided by the Subordinate Judge, 2nd Court, Barishal and the other papers connected thereto. In order to appreciate the arguments of both the parties let us have a look into the evidence on record.

34. Abul Kashem Molla as PW 1 deposed that Title Suit No. 40 of 1954 was filed in the Court of 2nd Subordinate Judge, Barishal for the land under RS khatian nos. 36 and 47 and in that suit he and his full sister Mominjan were the defendant nos. 12 and 13 and in that suit they got a decree on 23.04.1954 for 10.80 acres of land, the said decree was made final on 12.8.1955, his sister Mominjan Bibi died leaving him and the defendant nos. 1 and 2, he has been possessing 8.48 acres of land of which WAPDA has acquired .305 acres of land and deducting the said .305 acres of land he will get decree for 8.18 acres of land.

35. He also stated that it is not a fact that they got a decree in Title Suit No. 190 of 1956. He filed the certified copy of RS khatian nos. 36 and 47 marked as exhibits 1 and 1(Ka) and the decree of Title Suit No. 40 of 1954 marked as exhibits-2 series. He also stated that they have brought the record of Title Suit No. 40 of 1954 before the trial Court.

36. In cross examination, he stated that defendant no. 1 is his full brother, the defendant no. 1 is entitled to get a saham for 2.42 acres of land. In cross examination by defendant nos. 18-21 he stated that there were many owners in the said two khatians, he cannot say the names of all owners but can say the name of Sattya Ranjan and Vabo Ranjan, the predecessor of defendant nos. 18- 21 is his brother, he (predecessor of defendant nos. 18-21) is also entitled to get the share of his sister. He also stated that they are 3 brothers and 4 sisters. He categorically stated that he cannot say whether they, the 3(three) full brothers and sister Mominjan took the settlement of the land or not. He cannot say whether they filed the Title Suit No. 190 of 1956. He denied the defendants suggestion that they all the 3 brothers and sisters have been possessing the suit land. He also stated that his brothers have been possessing the land forcibly.

37. PW 2, Akter Peda told that both the parties are known to him, he has land adjacent to the suit land and the plaintiff has been possessing the land. In cross examination by the defendant nos. 18-21 he stated that he cannot say the exact area which is being possessed by the plaintiff, the defendant nos. 18-21 have also been possessing the land and all the 3 brothers are in possession of the suit land.

38. PW 3 Abdul Aziz Molla told that all the parties are known to him, the plaintiff has been possessing 8.18 acres of land, the plaintiff got decree in Title Suit No. 40 of 1954. In cross examination by defendant nos. 18-21 he stated that the Hindu Babus were the plaintiff in Title Suit No. 40 of 1954 and the tenants that is the raiyot were the defendants in the suit, he cannot say the name of the parties, defendant Delowar is known to him. They have been possessing their land also.

39. DW 1 for the defendant no. 1, Md. Forkan Majid deposing in the Court prayed for saham for 2.42 acres of land in favour of defendant no. 1. In cross examination by the defendant nos. 18-21 he stated that his father and uncle are 3 brothers and 4 sisters, they are Abdul Hamid, Hafizur Rahman and Abul Kashem Molla, his father has been possessing the land, he cannot say whether their father and uncles filed any suit after the decree of Title Suit No. 40 of 1954, in the suit land the plaintiff, and the predecessor of defendants nos. 18-21 have dwelling huts.

40. DW 2, Montu Mridha was examined on behalf of the defendant no. 1 to prove the possession of the defendant no. 1 Hafizur Rahman.

41. DW 3 Md. Delowar Hossain was examined on behalf of the defendant nos. 18-21 who deposed that he is defendant no. 18 and defendant nos. 19-21 is his sisters, 22.76 acres of land were recorded in RS khatian nos. 36 and 47, the said lands were in the schedule of Title Suit No. 40 of 1954 in the said suit his father Abdul Hamid and his uncle Hafiz were not made party, thereafter his father and uncles jointly filed Title Suit No. 190 of 1956, the said suit was decreed on compromise and pursuant to the decree of Title Suit No. 190 of 1956 their predecessors have been possessing the suit land now, they have been possessing the suit land and they have homestead on the suit land. He filed the plaint, petition of compromise and judgment and decree of Title Suit No. 190 of 1956 marked as exhibits 'Ka' series. He stated that it is not fact that the plaintiff has been possessing the suit land pursuant to the decree of Title Suit No. 40 of 1954.

42. In cross examination by the plaintiff he stated that no suit was filed for setting aside the decree of Title Suit No. 40 of 1954 but Title Suit No. 190 of 1956 was filed jointly. They purchased some land from Altu.

43. These are the evidences that have been given by the plaintiff and the defendants of the original suit. From the judgment of the trial Court it appears that the trial Court relied much upon the decree of Title Suit No. 40 of 1954 and considered the said decree thereof as an admitted suit in favour of the plaintiff and accepted the arguments of the plaintiff that the certified of the decree and other papers of Title Suit No. 190 of 1956 was created through forgery for the purpose of the present suit.

44. But unfortunately, the trial Court did not consider the evidence regarding the possession of the suit land adduced by the parties. Had the evidence relating to possession of the parties is considered the trial Court would have found that the defendant nos. 18-21 are in possession of the suit land along with the late plaintiff Abul Kashem Molla and then trial Court could have realized that the decree of Title Suit No. 190 of 1956 has been acted upon among the parties.

45. PW 1 Abul Kashem Molla, the plaintiff of the original suit himself stated in his evidence in the following ways:

“মামলার জমি আমরা তিন ভাই ও মমিনজান একত্রে পত্তন নেই কিনা জানিনা।”

46. And this is the case of the defendant nos. 18-21 that the 3(three) full brothers Abdul Hamid, Hafizur Rahman, Abul Kashem Molla and their sister Mominjan took the settlement of the suit land jointly. This case has not been denied by the plaintiff late Abul Kashem Molla or in other sense he could not deny the same.

47. The reality regarding the possession of all the co-sharers and the effectiveness of the decree of Title Suit No. 190 of 1956 has been revealed from the following evidence of PW 1 Abul Kashem Molla who stated in his evidence in the following manner:

“আমার ভাইয়েরা জমি জোর জুলুম করিয়া খায়। এই সকল কথা গোপন করিয়া ভাইদের সম্পত্তি আত্মসাৎ করার জন্য মিথ্যা মামলা করি সত্য না।”

48. The above evidence of PW 1 was enough to hold that all the 3 brothers ( Abdul Hamid, Hafizur Rahman and Abul Kashem Molla) and Mominjan have been possessing the suit land which ultimately established the case of the defendant nos. 18-21 that 3(three) full brothers and sister Mominjan took the settlement of the suit land jointly.

49. Pursuant to the decree of Title Suit No. 190 of 1956, the same type of evidence regarding the possession of all 3 brothers have been echoed by the evidence of PW 2, Akter Peada, PW 3 Abdul Aziz Mollah. PW 2 Akter Peda in his cross examination stated in the following ways:

১৮-২১ নং বিবাদী পক্ষ নালিশী জমা জমি ভোগ দখল করে। তিন ভাই দখলে আছে।

50. PW 3 Abdul Aziz Molla in his evidence stated in the following ways:

“বিবাদী দেলোয়ারকে চিনি। দেলোয়ারদের ১৮-২০ নং বিবাদীর বাড়ি ঘর আছে। দেলোয়ারদের জমি দেলোয়াররা জমি খায়।”

51. The plaintiff examined PWs 2 and 3 to prove his exclusive possession but they have strongly supported the possession of 3 brothers and their sister Mominjan Bibi.

52. The plaintiff could not assert strongly that the defendant nos. 18-21 have been possessing the suit land by purchase it from one Altu but the trial Court unfortunately tried to establish the said fact through his judgment. The trial Court did not consider the evidence regarding possession of the suit lands impartially, salter the trial Court for the reasons best known to him wrongly assessed the evidence regarding the possession of the defendant nos. 18-21 in the suit land. He introduced a fact not supported by the materials on record.

53. The trial Court relied much upon the decree of Title Suit No. 40 of 1954 as its original record was called for. From the record of Title Suit No. 40 of 1954 it appears that the said suit was filed on 12.04.1954 for 106.60 acres of land and before the date of service of summons all the defendants appeared and filed solenama on 15.04.1954 within 3 days of its filing and the suit was decreed on 23.04.1954 within 11 days and the decree was made final on 26.04.1954 within 14 days. Now is it not enough to consider the category of the decree of Title Suit No. 40 of 1954. From the date of its filing the suit was decreed within 14 days although the suit was related for 106.00 acres of land.

54. Over and again, Abul Kashem Molla and Mominjan did not file the said suit. There was a narration about their portion made by others and the suit was decreed as it is. From a decree of this nature it can safely be said that all the activities relating to filing of the suit, appearance of the parties, filing of solenama and the decrees were made as part of a design, though there was a saham in favour of Abul Kashem Molla and Mominjan Bibi but that might have been done by others to save their interest having no knowledge of Abul Kashem Molla and Mominjan (defendant nos. 12/13 of Title suit no. 40 of 1954 and it is clear from the evidence of PW 1 himself and others that the decree of Title Suit No. 40 of 1954 has not been acted upon for the suit land. Had it been acted upon, the suit land would have been possessed by Abul Kashem Mollah and Mominjan Bibi only but PW 1 clearly stated in his evidence that his other brothers have been possessing the suit land forcefully which ultimately indicates that all the brothers have been in possession of the suit land pursuant to the decree of Title Suit No. 190 of 1956 and not pursuant to the decree of Title Suit No. 40 of 1954. Moreover, by filing subsequent Title Suit No. 190 of 1956 and obtaining decree in that suit Abdul Kashem Mollah admitted his other brothers as owners of the property.

55. The appellate Court below made a great ditto to the judgment of the trial Court without perusing his own record. Before pronouncing judgment by the appellate Court below on 20.03.2008, the record of Title Suit No. 190 of 1956 was tagged with the record of Title Appeal No. 11 of 2006, but the Appellate Court below failed to appreciate that fact and did not peruse the record of Title Suit No. 190 of 1956. From the order dated 10.03.2008 it appears that the Appellate Court below received the record of Title Suit No. 190 of 1956 on that day. The order of Title Appeal No. 11 of 2006 dated 10.03.2008 runs as follows:

“২৬ ১(ক)-১(ঝ) ও ২(ক)-২(ঝ) ২০/২১ নং রেসপন্ডেট পক্ষ হাজিরা দেন। দেওয়ানী ১৯০/৫৬ নং মামলার নথি পাওয়া গেল। উহা নথি সামিলে রাখা হইল। আপীলকারী পক্ষ শুনানীর জন্য সময়ের প্রার্থনা করেন। শুনলাম। প্রার্থনা না মঞ্জুর করা গেল। আপীলকারীপক্ষ হাজিরা দেন। মোকদ্দমা শুনানীর জন্য লওয়া হইল। শুনলাম। আগামী ২০.০৩.২০০৮ তারিখ রায়।”

56. From the above order dated 10.03.2008 in Title Appeal No. 11 of 2006 it appears that the original record of Title Suit No. 190 of 1956 was tagged with the appeal in question on 10.03.2008 and obviously, the defendant nos. 18-21 rightly called for the record of Title Suit No. 190 of 1956 for the adverse observations of the Trial Court that the original record of Title Suit No. 190 of 1956 was not called for and the certified copy of the said suit might have been created by means of forgery by the defendant nos. 18-21 and for the aforesaid reasons the trial Court did not believe the decree of Title Suit No. 90 of 1956. The defendants appellants to remove all sorts of confusion regarding the genuines of the decree of Title suit no. 190 of 1956 rightly called for the original records of Title suit no. 190 of 1956 for perusal by the appellate Court below.

57. However, since the original record of Title Suit No. 190 of 1956 was tagged on 10.03.2008 with the appeal, the appellant prayed for time for hearing of the appeal but that was not allowed by the Appellate Court. In my consideration the appellate Court below should have allowed the adjournment petition giving a short time to the appellant for placing the record of Title Suit No. 190 of 1956 which shows the non-application of judicial mind of the Judge of the Appellate Court below in disposing the appeal.

<u>58. However, be that as it may, from the judgment of appellate Court below it is crystal clear that the appellate Court did not peruse the record of Title Suit No. 190 of 1956 and from the judgment it further appears that it was not within the knowledge and notice of the appellate Court below that the record of</u>

<u>Title Suit No. 190 of 1956 was available before him for his perusal and it would be clear from the judgment of the appellate Court below itself. The appellate Court below in the last portion of the judgment made observations in the following way:</u>

<u>“বিজ্ঞ নিম্নাদালত দেওয়ানী ১৯০/৫৬ নং মামলার সংশ্লিষ্ট কাগজ পত্রের জাবেদা নকল পর্যালোচনা করেছেন। ঐ মামলার আরজি হতে দেখা যায় যে, তাতে দেওয়ানী ৪০/৫৪ নং মামলার বিবরন রয়েছে। ঐ মোকদ্দমার মাধ্যমে স্বত্ব ঘোষনার প্রার্থনা করা হয় এবং সোলে সূত্রে ডিক্রি অর্জন করা হয়। বাদী রেসপন্ডেন্ট পক্ষ ঐ কাগজী প্রমান সমূহ জাল জালিয়াতী মর্মে সৃষ্টি বলে দাবী করেন। এ প্রসঙ্গে বিজ্ঞ নিম্নাদালত অভিমত পোষন করেন যে, সাধারনত কোন সরকারী দলিলের জাবেদা নকল সাক্ষ্য হিসাবে গ্রহণ করা হলেও তর্কিত ঐ নথী তলব করে ঐ মামলার বিষয় বস্তু প্রমান করা আবশ্যক ছিল। উপরন্ত দেওয়ানী ১৯০/৫৬ নং মামলার পূর্ববর্তী ৪০/৫৪ নং বন্টনের মামলার ডিক্রির বিষয় কোন প্রতিকার প্রার্থনা না করায় বিবাদী পক্ষে দাখিলকৃত ডিক্রি মূলে বিবাদীপক্ষের স্বত্ব দখল অনুমান করা যায় না। বিজ্ঞ নিম্নাদালতের এই আইনী বিশ্লেষন এবং অভিমত সঠিক ও সমর্থনযোগ্য।”</u>

<u>59. From the above noted observations of the appellate Court it appears that the trial Court did not consider the decree of Title Suit No. 190 of 1956 as genuine as its original record was not called for and also made a blind endorsement to the said observations of the Trial Court although on the very date of pronouncement of the judgment the original record of Title Suit No. 190 of 1956 was lying with the record of the Title Appeal No. 11 of 2006 and it is a serious non-application of judicial mind on the part of the appellate Court.</u>

60. The record of Title Suit No. 190 of 1956 shows that this suit was filed on 28.05.1956 by 3 brothers Abdul Hamid, Abul Kashem Molla and Hafizur Rahman along with Mominjan Bibi, that is, by 3(three) full brothers and one sister. Solenama was filed on 11.12.1956 and decree was passed on 18.12.1956.The time for disposal of the suit appears to be rational. Over and again, in the said suit (Title Suit No. 190 of 1956) there is a statement that through in Title Suit No. 40 of 1954 the landlord admitted the claim of the plaintiffs which ultimately establishes that the claim of the 3 brothers and one sister as made in was not contradictory with the claim of Title Suit No. 40 of 1954.

<u>61. I have stated it earlier that Title Suit No. 40 of 1954 was not filed by Abul Kashem Molla and his sister Mominjan rather it was filed by some other persons. Whenever the 3 brothers and one sister filed a subsequent suit being Title Suit No. 190 of 1956 where their title in the suit land has been declared the decree and the judgment passed in Title Suit No. 190 of 1956 appears to be more genuine and rational and binding upon the plaintiffs, the 3 brothers and one sister and there is no scope to deny the judgment and decree of Title Suit No. 190 of 1956.</u>

<u>62. More so, it is not natural and probable that with any ill motive or for some illegal gain in the year 1956 a suit was filed in the name of 3 brothers and one sister. Abul Kashem Molla filed the present suit in the year of 2001. It is unthinkable that 45 years ago a suit was filed for any other purpose without any genuine reasons. Since the 3 brothers and 1 sister acquired the suit land from the landlord and since a suit which was filed by some other persons which was decreed against the interest of the two remaining brothers namely Hafizur Rahman and Abdul Hamid, all the 3 brothers and 1 sister to have a genuine declaration regarding their title filed the Title Suit No. 190 of 1956 and from the evidence of PW 1 (plaintiff Abul Kashem Mollah) that his other brothers have been possessing the suit land forcibly is very much significant in this Rule and ultimately has strengthened the decree of Title Suit No. 190 of 1956 in all the ways.</u>

63. If the evidence of PW 1 is considered along with the decree of Title Suit No. 190 of 1956 it would be clear that pursuant to the decree of Title Suit No. 190 of 1956 all the 3 brothers and sister have been possessing the suit land. Over and again, in this Rule, the petitioners filed an application for taking additional evidence to prove that pursuant to the decree of Title Suit No. 190 of 1956 the name of 3 brothers and 1 sister have been mutated through Mutation Case No. 25 of 1961.This small piece of paper is enough to hold that the decree of Title Suit No. 190 of 1956 has been acted upon among the 3 brothers and 1 sister.

<u>64. However, be that as it may, I find that both the trial Court and appellate Court below without considering the evidence and other materials on record came to a very wrong and illegal conclusion that Abul Kashem Molla and Mominjan Bibi got the suit land through the decree in Title Suit No. 40 of 1954.The appellate Court below without considering the evidence on record and without going through the records of Title Suit No. 190 of 1956 made a simple ditto to the judgment of the trial Court which cannot be appreciated rather I deprecate the attitude and non application of judicial mind and non consideration of important materials on record by the appellate Court below.</u>

65. Under the above facts and circumstances, the judgments and the decrees passed by the trial Court and the appellate Court below are suffering from gross illegality which cannot be sustained at all but since this is a suit for partition and since the petitioner also filed an application in this Rule for saham, I am of the view that the same deserves consideration.

66. Generally, a revisional Court did not reverse the concurrent findings of the Courts below based on proper evidence (62 DLR (AD) 242 Abdul Gafur Vs. Md. Abdur Razzak). But in many cases it has been held that the concurrent findings of the Court below cannot claim immunity if the very basis of the concurrent, findings of the two Courts below appears to be based on misconception, on misreading of evidence or non consideration of materials on record such concurrent findings cannot claim any immunity (40 DLR (AD) 62 Mozer Sowdagar Vs. Md. Zahirul Alam).

67. In the Case of Abdul Mazid Howlader Vs. Lehajuddin Howlader 16 BLD (AD) 197 it has been held that a revisional Court may interfere in the concurrent findings of the fact of the Courts below when there appears misreading of evidence, wrong appreciation of the evidence, non consideration of oral and documentary evidence by the Courts below and when the findings of the Courts below are found to be perverse and not based on the evidence on record which resulted into an error in the decisions occasioning failure of justice.

68. In this Rule, it has been found earlier that the Courts below did not consider the evidence of possession of the defendant petitioners although their possession has been strongly supported by the witnesses of the plaintiff himself and the record of Title Suit No. 190 of 1956 which was called for, for perusal of the appellate Court below and though the said record came before the appellate Court below before the pronouncement of judgment, the appellate Court below did not consider the same rather made a great ditto to the judgment of the trial Court.

69. The appellate Court below did not also consider the evidence on record independently. The appellate Court below gave the blow to the wind raised by the trial Court simply. So the judgment of the Courts below cannot claim any immunity from this Court rather for the ends of justice the same are liable to be set aside.

70. As it appears from the record that the original suit was a suit for partition. The defendant nos.18-21 happens to be one of the co-sharer in the suit land and during hearing of this Rule they filed two separate petition, first one, is for the amendment of the written statements and the second one, is for, separate saham.

71. In the case of Naiyum Vs. Rahima Khatun 42 DLR 523 it has been held that the provision of Order 6 Rule 17 of the Code is applicable both for plaint and written statement and when a proposed amendment of the written statement does not change the fundamental character of the defence it is liable to be allowed.

72. In the case of 50 DLR (AD) 86 it has been held by our Apex Court that amendment may be allowed when it is necessary for the determination of the real question in controversy between the parties and does not change the character of the suit. Obviously by the proposed amendment of the written statement the nature of the suit and their claim would not be changed.

73. In the case of Abu Shafiq Vs. Asaduzzaman 9 BLT 359 it has been held by this division that a prayer for amendment should be considered liberally for bringing all possible controversies between the parties for complete and effective adjudication and avoid multification of litigations.

74. Having regards to the above decisions I am of the view that though the prayer for amendment of written statement has been filed at this stage, the same should be considered to adjudicate the real dispute between the parties and in the case of Kajol Das Vs. Monowara 8 BLC 414 it was held that the amendment of pleadings may be granted at any stage even in the appeal, or in revision. Since the original suit was a partition suit and since it has been found that the contesting defendant nos. 18-21 are co-sharer of the plaintiff for the suit land I am of the view that the ends of justice would be best served if the suit is sent back on remand for fresh trial by setting aside the judgment of both the Courts below giving an opportunity to the defendant nos.18-21 to seek the amendment in the trial Court and along with the prayer for saham and the trial Court will consider the same in accordance with the law.

75. In the result, the Rule is made absolute. The judgment and decree dated 20.03.2008 passed in Title Appeal No. 11 of 2006 are hereby set aside and consequently the judgment and decree dated 13.11.2005., passed in the Title Suit No.16 of 2001 by the Joint District Judge, 1st Court, Patuakhali is also set aside. Title Suit No. 16 of 2001 is sent back on remand to the trial Court for trial afresh.

76. The trial Court should consider the amendment petition and the prayer for saham if the party concerned seeks the same. The trial Court is directed to dispose of the suit in the light of the observations made hereinabove, within a shortest possible time preferably within 6 months from the date of receipt of the judgment. Parties to the suit will be at liberty to adduce more evidence along with evidence adduced earlier if they desire.

77. Original documents filed by the petitioner with application for taking as additional evidence be returned to the petitioners to enable them to file the same before the trial court providing photocopies of the same.

78. There will be no order as to costs.

79. Order of Stay granted at the time of issuance of the Rule Stands vacated.

80. Communicate a copy of this judgment and send down the lower court records at once.

End.
